findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime sort keys
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint uses this paginator with order_by='-datetime', so getattr(item, self.key) returns a datetime. get_item_key passes that datetime directly to math.floor/math.ceil, which raises TypeError. DateTimePaginator avoids this by converting via strftime and a multiplier. Consequently build_cursor's key calls fail and the optimized audit-log path returns a 500 whenever a page contains results.

findings.title: value_from_cursor does not convert cursor timestamps to datetime
findings.body: value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged. For the audit-log endpoint the cursor value must be interpreted as a datetime timestamp and converted to an aware datetime, as DateTimePaginator does; instead the raw numeric value is passed to BasePaginator.build_queryset and used in the datetime column comparison in queryset.extra(where=["...datetime <= %s"]). Subsequent pages will therefore filter incorrectly or fail at the database layer, so cursor navigation cannot work even if get_item_key is fixed.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch uses unsupported negative QuerySet slicing
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, the code executes list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing and raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically. A crafted or generated negative cursor therefore crashes the request instead of providing reverse pagination.

findings.title: BasePaginator change only clamps negative offsets for non-prev cursors
findings.body: In the shared BasePaginator.get_result used by many endpoints, start_offset is clamped with max(0, offset) only when cursor.is_prev is false; for prev cursors the raw offset is still used as queryset[start_offset:stop]. A user-supplied cursor such as 'value:-1:1' parsed by Cursor.from_string therefore still reaches Django with a negative slice index and raises AssertionError, producing a 500. The change is inconsistent and leaves the claimed negative-offset handling unsafe in the common paginator.

findings.title: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit-log path
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class, changes shared BasePaginator slicing, and adds a new query-param-gated branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but adds no tests. In particular there is no test exercising OptimizedCursorPaginator with a datetime key, a second-page cursor, a prev cursor, or a negative offset, which would have caught the datetime conversion and negative-slicing failures before merge.
